title: The use of aspirational language, such as the word 'dream', may predict slower funding.
Female borrowers using descriptive character traits like 'brave', 'inspiring', or 'hardworking' may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who provide specific personal demographics, such as the number of children, fund faster.
Female borrowers who list specific retail inventory, such as canned goods and chips, may fund faster.
Female borrowers who use descriptors like 'hardworking' or 'works very hard' may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention preparing land for farming may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a goal to expand the business may fund faster.
Female borrowers who describe personal hardships, such as displacement, may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who specify the loan amount in local currency may fund faster.
Female borrowers who list specific product ingredients or inventory items may fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention sustaining business through past NWTF loans fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning the education of children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
